canonicalChecks.classification: lexical source binding, not dynamic reachability/equivalence

sourceReasoning.reasoning: For connected DAG n>1, every original source has positive outdegree and enters the source FIFO; every non-original-source has positive indegree. Sink removal only decreases unprocessed predecessors outdegree. Since the residual graph is acyclic, all non-original-sources eventually enter the sink FIFO once; source insertion after target indegree change cannot occur during this sink-only drain. The sink-add indegree>0 condition excludes all original sources. Source FIFO is then drained; no max-outflow fallback remains.

Sink sequence marks are -1,-2,...; shifting by n+1 reverses sink-removal order to increasing edge order above all k original sources. Original sources get1..k in their FIFO work order. Isolated singleton uses the initial sink branch, shifts to1. For every edge predecessor mark<target, so reverse/CYCLIC writes are unreachable; body still performs the actual reversal-check iteration.

Default priority0 gives integer edge contribution1, degree<=7 and total edges<=28 for simple n<=8 DAG. Marks and counters remain bounded exact integers. Reading RANDOM does not draw from it; chooseNodeWithMaxOutflow is guarded out by the queue proof, not by missing coverage. Incoming-before-outgoing and mutable-list iteration order remain source obligations.

The inherited E04 source/helper disposition table is bound by artifact SHA and a resolving JSON pointer. Queue/list/identity/property/scalar defaults stay the same host mappings. E05 explicitly does not inherit path-only algorithm proof. New observer helper names are instrumentation query overhead, not new unmodified-source GREEDY logic.

limitations: Approval is for this one pre-layering NORMAL DAG component, not BARYCENTER/BK/ORTHO or whole E05.
